name: Two Truths and a Lie

scoring.report_note: Report room-level deltas only; individual answers stay private — this is an icebreaker, not an exam.

description: One-minute pre/post measure for the Two Truths and a Lie icebreaker. Scores per person: how much of the room you actually got to know — recall, not cleverness.

instructions.pre: Before the circle forms. Each person answers alone, about the team they work with every day — the usual, not the game.
instructions.post: Immediately after the light debrief. Same items, now answered about this session.

items.pre_text: I can name three checkable facts about each colleague I work with daily.
items.post_text: I now hold at least three new facts about a colleague from this room.

items.pre_text: My first read of a colleague holds until it is proven wrong.
items.post_text: During the voting, one of my confident reads proved wrong — and I enjoyed it.

items.pre_text: When a fact about a colleague surprises me, I ask a follow-up question.
items.post_text: A surprise in this game became a question I asked out loud.

items.pre_text: Sharing work facts about myself in a group is easy for me.
items.post_text: Saying my three statements in the circle was easy.

report.title: Two Truths and a Lie — recall delta
sections: One suggested follow-up conversation per participant, from the largest positive delta
